title: Pytest Fixtures Scope
prompt_markdown: In pytest, what is the default scope of a `@pytest.fixture` if no `scope` argument is provided?
hints: Is it per session, per module, or per function?

content.explanation: By default, pytest fixtures have `scope="function"`, meaning they are re-created for every individual test function to ensure test isolation.

title: Pytest Parametrization
prompt_markdown: Which pytest decorator is used to execute a single test function across multiple sets of input arguments and expected outputs?

content.explanation: `@pytest.mark.parametrize("arg,expected", [(1, 2), (2, 3)])` runs the test function once for each parameter tuple, reporting clear per-case test statuses.

title: Deterministic Tests Rule in Forge
prompt_markdown: Why must automated test suites never make live network calls to third-party APIs or Gemini LLMs?
hints: Flakiness, latency, cost, and AGENTS.md rule.

rubric: Mentions test non-determinism/flakiness due to network and model variance.
Mentions cost, rate limits, and latency.
Mentions using mock objects or fake providers to test business logic deterministically.
content.reference_answer: Live API calls introduce non-determinism: network latency, unexpected outages, API rate limits, and non-deterministic LLM responses can cause random test failures (flakiness). Furthermore, they incur dollar costs and leak secrets. In automated testing, engineers inject fake providers or mock responses to ensure 100% deterministic, instant, reproducible test verification of application logic.

title: Testing Boundary and Edge Conditions
prompt_markdown: When testing a function that processes numerical intervals or string inputs, what specific boundary cases must always be included?

rubric: Lists empty inputs (empty string, empty list).
Lists null/None values or invalid data types.
Lists extreme boundary values (zero, negative numbers, max integer, exact boundary fence-posts).
content.reference_answer: Essential boundary cases include: 1) Empty inputs (empty string `""`, empty list `[]`); 2) Zero and negative values (0, -1); 3) Exact boundary values (off-by-one points at minimum and maximum ranges, e.g. indices 0 and len-1); 4) Null/None or malformed data to ensure proper validation errors or graceful handling; 5) Single-element collections.
